From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@brightworks.com>

Subject: Clarify product title & training blacklist in attached MSA redlines

Irene —

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the MSA. We've circulated the attached redlines and have two outstanding asks we need clarified before procurement can approve:

1) Product title / output ownership: our commercial team needs a formal acknowledgement that BrightWorks will retain title to customer-generated output used directly in our product (examples: curated QA dataset exported from your API).
   - We don't expect assignment of Redwood's underlying model weights, but we need explicit language that BrightWorks retains ownership of outputs for our productization.

2) Training blacklist / feedback license: legal flagged the feedback license in section 7.4 as broad. We need either an explicit opt-out mechanism for "designated content" and confirmation that Redwood will not use designated customer-proprietary inputs for model training without separate consent.

We attached a sample Exhibit A (provenance fields) showing the metadata we would like documented for any retained-output evidence. See attachments.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept narrow language that: (A) confirms customer title to outputs for their product use, and (B) accepts a training opt-out for specified data classes (PII, HIPAA PHI, and customer-tagged proprietary content)? If not, can you propose alternative contractual language?

Elena — procurement asked for an estimate of how long an internal legal review would take if we receive Redwood's proposed redline tomorrow.

Appreciate the help — we are trying to keep this on the quarter-close timeline.

Attachments: BrightWorks_MSA_redlines.pdf (redlines), exhibitA-provenance.xlsx (fields sample)

—Samir
Samir Patel
Senior Counsel, Contracts | BrightWorks

Subject: Re: Clarify product title & training blacklist in attached MSA redlines

Samir / Elena —

Thanks for the clear note and the exhibit. Short answer: we can accept a narrowly scoped customer title acknowledgement for customer-generated outputs, and we can operationalize a training opt-out for "designated content" categories, with some implementation details to work through.

High-level positions for us:
- Output/title: Redwood will not claim ownership of Customer output used directly in Customer's product (we will propose language that distinguishes "Customer Product Output" from model IP and derivative model weights).
- Training opt-out: we can provide a contractual opt-out that prevents using designated content for model training or evaluation; we will need a mechanism for customers to tag data or provide an exclusions manifest (Exhibit A style).

Open items we want to coordinate on:
1) Definition of "designated content" — proposal: PII/PHI (we can accept standard definitions), and customer-proprietary content that BrightWorks flags via the exclusions manifest.
2) Evidence & auditability — how much provenance metadata do you need to rely on the exclusion (your Exhibit A).
3) Operational latency — opting out will affect the pool of telemetry we use for quality monitoring; we should document fallbacks for safety telemetry.

Internal next steps: looping in Legal (Laura), Contracts/Procurements (Ben), and Product Compliance (Hannah) to draft specific redline language and an Exhibit A template. I'll aim to return proposed redlines by Monday EOD PST.

If the timeline is tight for quarter close, please flag which item (title vs training opt-out) is higher priority.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: FW: Clarify product title & training blacklist in attached MSA redlines — proposed language

Quick internal note — drafting guidance below that I would include in our response to BrightWorks. Happy to refine.

Proposed clause snippets (for redlines):
1) "Customer Product Output": "Customer retains all right, title and interest in and to outputs generated solely by Customer-provided inputs and metadata that Customer uses or incorporates into Customer's own products or services, subject to the license rights expressly granted to Redwood for performance and support."

2) Training Opt-Out / Exclusions Manifest: "Customer may designate classes of content ("Excluded Content") via Exhibit A. Redwood will not incorporate Excluded Content into model training or evaluation datasets, and will exclude such content from automated model improvement processes. Redwood shall maintain reasonable technical controls and records demonstrating exclusion, and shall provide a summary report on request subject to confidentiality limits."

3) Limitations/Operations note: We should include a carveout for aggregated and de-identified telemetry used solely for safety and to prevent model regressions (with minimum aggregation thresholds), and a mutual commitment not to use proprietary source data for public model releases.

Attachments: I'll ping Laura for legal polish and Hannah for operational feasibility.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Contracts Manager | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarify product title & training blacklist in attached MSA redlines — Redwood position + next steps

Samir / Elena —

Appreciate the patience. We've coordinated with Legal and Product Compliance and can commit to the following as our preferred, pragmatic compromise:

1) Output ownership: Redwood will accept an express acknowledgement that Customer retains title to Customer Product Output (as defined in the redline language we will attach). This does not transfer model ownership, weights, or Redwood proprietary components.

2) Training opt-out: BrightWorks may supply an "Exclusions Manifest" (Exhibit A) listing Disallowed Classes and specific assets. Redwood will exclude those assets from training/evaluation datasets and from automated feedback ingestion. Excluded data will still be used for operational telemetry in an aggregated, de-identified form sufficient for service stability unless BrightWorks specifically requests additional restrictions.

3) Evidence & reporting: Redwood will produce a one-time provenance summary for onboarding and will provide an annual summary of exclusion compliance on request (subject to redaction for internal tooling).

4) Implementation timeline: we will deliver redline text for the MSA and an Exhibit A template to BrightWorks legal by Tue 2026-11-10 COB PST. Ben and Laura will shepherd final legal polish; Hannah will validate operational feasibility and any safety telemetry carveouts.

Action items / owners:
- Ben Carter: prepare final contract redline language (deliverable: annotated redline) — due Tue COB 2026-11-10.
- Laura Bennett: legal sign-off / comments — due Wed 2026-11-11.
- Hannah Schmitt: operations feasibility & note on telemetry carveouts — due Tue 2026-11-10.
- Irene Choi: send redlines and Exhibit A template to BrightWorks; coordinate procurement timing.

Samir — if that captures your needs at a high level, we'll follow up with the precise language tomorrow. If procurement needs an ETA on how long internal BrightWorks review will take, let us know and we'll prioritize.

Thanks —
Irene
